Testing if prioritizing models with lower historical error can mitigate the impact of unstable rankings in this trend-dominated regime.
Testing if concentrating weight on high-performing models via softmax improves performance in this highly predictable, trend-dominated series, despite ranking instability.
Testing shape-based aggregation to address unstable ranking tau in a trend-dominated regime.
Testing median to handle unstable ranking tau in a trend-dominated regime.
Testing softmax weighting on the full pool to see if it handles the unstable ranking and trend-dominated regime better than inverse error or temporal weights.
Testing simple mean as a baseline against unstable ranking tau.
Testing a concentrated subset (pool1) with softmax weighting to mitigate unstable ranking tau.
Testing a concentrated subset (pool1) with inverse_error weighting to mitigate the effects of unstable ranking tau.
Testing trimmed mean on pool5 to see if it provides more robustness than weighted combination in this trend-dominated regime.

The current leader (a9) uses a specific weighted combination on pool5; given the unstable ranking tau and the trend-dominated regime, I want to test if a shape-based aggregation (DBA) on the same highly-ranked subset (pool1) can provide better robustness than error-based weighting.
Testing softmax weighting on pool5 to see if it handles the unstable ranking and high variance better than inverse error weighting.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool5 weighted by w6' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9581. Series context: trend strength 0.9595 and seasonal strength 0.4048; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.099); 2 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.427.
